title: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
content:
Google would certainly prefer that everyone used its Gemini models with Google Cloud services, but soon, you’ll have more options. OpenAI and Google have come to an arrangement that will see the former’s frontier models arrive in Google Cloud services. Perhaps more importantly, GPT models will soon appear in Antigravity, Google’s agent-powered coding tool.
For enterprise customers and AI enthusiasts, OpenAI’s latest model will appear in Google’s “Model Garden” in the coming weeks, adding to its 200-plus options. The garden already offers access to Google’s Gemini models, as well as an assortment of open models like Mistral, Llama, and Gemma. Anthropic’s Claude AI has also been available for some time. Google says it’s now the only large cloud provider offering access to all three leading closed LLMs.
While OpenAI notes that Microsoft continues to be its primary cloud partner, the full suite of current GPT 6 and 6.1 models—Astra, Sol, and Luna—will launch on Google Cloud. Astra will naturally cost the most to run, but Google’s system supports dynamically moving workloads between LLMs based on performance, latency, and efficiency.
OpenAI models will be available to run entirely on Google’s infrastructure, with transactions handled via the Google Cloud Marketplace. For businesses with established Google Cloud spending commitments, this will make it easy to begin using GPT models in place of whatever they were using before.

report.summary: OpenAI’s GPT-6 and 6.1 models are coming to Google Cloud’s Model Garden and Antigravity, giving enterprises a new way to access frontier models alongside Gemini and Claude.
report.background: Cloud providers have increasingly competed on model choice, not just infrastructure. Enterprises want to avoid locking critical AI workloads to a single vendor, while model developers want broader distribution. Google’s Model Garden already hosts Gemini, Anthropic’s Claude and many open models, positioning Google Cloud as a marketplace. OpenAI, meanwhile, has Microsoft as its primary cloud partner but is expanding access through other channels. The deal reflects a broader shift toward multi-cloud AI procurement: customers want to compare models, route workloads dynamically and use existing cloud spending commitments. It also puts pressure on AWS, which may need similar arrangements to match Google’s “all three leading closed LLMs” pitch.
key_points: Google Cloud’s Model Garden will add OpenAI’s current GPT-6 and 6.1 models—Astra, Sol and Luna—within weeks. That brings its catalog to more than 200 models and lets Google claim it is the only major cloud provider offering all three leading closed LLMs: Gemini, Claude and GPT.

The more strategic piece is Antigravity, Google’s agent-powered coding tool. GPT models will appear inside it, giving developers model choice within agentic coding workflows rather than forcing them to leave Google’s environment for OpenAI access. That could make Antigravity more competitive with Cursor, GitHub Copilot and other AI coding tools.

Enterprise buyers can run OpenAI models entirely on Google infrastructure and pay through Google Cloud Marketplace. Businesses with existing Google Cloud spending commitments can more easily adopt GPT models, potentially replacing other models without new procurement cycles. This lowers friction for adoption.

Google says its system can dynamically move workloads between LLMs based on performance, latency and efficiency. Astra, the most capable GPT variant, will cost the most to run, so routing could help customers balance quality against cost. That is a key advantage of a multi-model marketplace.

OpenAI says Microsoft remains its primary cloud partner. The Google deal is therefore an expansion, not a switch. It shows OpenAI wants distribution across major clouds, while Google is willing to host a rival’s frontier models to win enterprise AI workloads.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the deal blurs the line between model makers and cloud platforms. Google is acting as a neutral marketplace even while promoting Gemini, and OpenAI is widening distribution without abandoning Microsoft. Enterprises gain leverage: they can compare GPT, Gemini and Claude inside one cloud, use existing commitments and route tasks by cost or latency. Developers get more model choice in Google’s tools, especially Antigravity, but must manage multi-model governance, data handling and unpredictable costs. Regular users may see better AI coding assistants and apps that pick models more intelligently, though the benefits will arrive first in enterprise products.
report.tools: Watch Google Cloud’s Model Garden and Antigravity for direct access. For multi-provider experimentation, try LiteLLM, an open-source proxy that standardizes OpenAI-compatible calls across models, and LangChain for model-agnostic workflows. Vertex AI’s model routing and evaluation tools are also worth following if you deploy on Google Cloud.
